inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that caregivers allow children to participate in screen time activities that are not related to planned activities that meet educational goals.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that staff failed to supervise children when children were pushing shelves and climbing on chairs and an infant stroller.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that a caregiver grabbed a child by the arm before picking them up and putting them in a restrictive device for time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that a child was placed in a restrictive device for time out for 42 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out (26 TAC §746.2805(8))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The operation did not have a current fire inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One caregiver did not have current training in pediatric first aid. The caregiver is scheduled to take the course on 9/4/25.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: One infant was sitting in a high chair without the safety strap fastened. This was corrected when the caregiver fastened the safety strap.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely: One vehicle had seat cushions that had rips and tears. Some of the vehicle's seatbelt mechanisms were missing the plastic piece that attaches to the back of the seat. One seat was repaired with duct tape around the area where the seatbelt comes out of the seat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Types of Vehicles Used to Transport Children - Be Maintained Safely (26 TAC §746.5603(c))

occurrences.finding: Required Immunizations: One child did not have updated immunizations. The child has an appointment scheduled for 1/20/25 to receive the required immunizations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Immunizations (26 TAC §746.613(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Immunizations: Two children were missing updated immunization records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Immunizations (26 TAC §746.613(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: One caregiver with direct access to children was present without an eligible background check. This was corrected when the caregiver left the operation during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Parent Rights: Five children records did not include a signed Parent's Rights Form 2987.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Parent Rights (26 TAC §746.501(a)(20))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985): Five out of ten personnel files were missing a notarized Affidavit for Employment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: Name to face checks are not being conducted consistently at 10,12,2,and 4 during the day, and cleaning checklists for the infant and pre-k rooms are not being completed daily.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: The operation failed to provide a parent an incident report within 48 hours of the incident occurring.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver was observed inappropriately grabbing a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: Four caregivers, with direct access to children, was present without a background check eligibility.  The caregiver was sent home during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: Two of the ten record reviewed were lacking the required immunizations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: Children in care that are not yet ready for table food were lacking feeding instructions.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Caregivers were lacking the required annual trainings.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child in care was in a room unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Caregivers in three of the five open classrooms were not aware of the number of children in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: During the investigation inspection walkthrough, the following things were observed.  - the entry way floor and classroom floors had trash particles and spill stain discoloration  - two garbage cans did not have lids, exposing the garbage to the children,  - classrooms, bathrooms, and hallways had peeling paint  - multiple tables were not sanitized after feeding leaving crumbs and other food particles on the table  - used toilet paper was found on the edge of the toilet seat and on top of the toilet paper dispensers  These things do not assist in maintaining the building and therefore does not protect the health of the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Children were observed watching television and eating breakfast.   The caregiver was informed of screen time requirements and the television was turned off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment: The restrooms were not cleaned and sanitized.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Sanitize Tables Tops, Furniture and Similar Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407(11))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: The operaton has paint peeling on several walls.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: It was found that a caregiver utilized prohibited punishment on a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: The operation did not notify parents after children were left unsupervised in a classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: Not all parents received an incident report when their child was left unattended.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation did not report to Child Care Regulation within the required 2 days when three children were left unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Caregivers yell at children as a form of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities - Not interfere with an inspection or investigation: A caregiver was instructed on what needed to be said to the Child Care Investigator.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities - Not interfere with an inspection or investigation (26 TAC §745.8411(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was allowed to go from the playground inside the classroom unattended to use the restroom. Three other children followed this child inside. The children were unsupervised for approximately ten minutes. During this time two children were running with safety scissors in their mouth and the children were going in between different classrooms.    Children are allowed to go from the playground inside the classroom unattended to use the restroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: A caregiver was observed telling a child they would not get their food if they did not sit in the chair.     Caregiver was asked to leave for the day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: A caregiver was observed  threatening children as a form of discipline.    This caregiver was asked to leave for the day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: During the investigation it was determined a caregiver yelled and humiliated children.    The caregiver was immediately terminated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: During the investigation it was determined a caregiver threatened children as a form of discipline.    The caregiver was immediately terminated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on information obtained during an investigation, it was determined that the childcare facility did not notify Licensing within the required timeframe regarding a situation that placed a child at risk when a caregiver grabbed a child by their shirt.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: There is enough evidence to support that a caregiver was grabbing and pushing children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: There is enough evidence to support that caregivers were yelling at children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety: There is enough evidence to support that a caregiver was not sufficiently intervening when children in care were interacting in rough manners with each other such as dog piling and wrestling with each other.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Foster Cooperative Atmosphere: There is enough evidence to support that a caregiver was telling children to hit other children back when children hit each other.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Foster Cooperative Atmosphere (26 TAC §746.1203(8))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: This standard was evaluated during the investigation and found out of compliance. A child was left unattended on the playground.       The standard was marked into compliance at the time of the inspection when all of the caregivers were observed supervising in compliance with minimum standards. The director stated the caregiver who left the child unattended was counseled and retrained on supervision.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection - Conducted Local Sanitation Official: A sanitation inspection was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection - Conducted Local Sanitation Official (26 TAC §746.3401(b))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal: The fire inspection was not avaiolable for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal (26 TAC §746.5101(b))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: There was no fire drill documentation for December or January. A fire drill was completed during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: A plastic slide that was on the playground was broken causing a shear point in the slide.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)
